defect_found_and_fixed.severity: the one tool whose entire job is 'who is around me' was hiding the neighbours that matter
defect_found_and_fixed.root_cause: the pot has two notions of 'in a squad' — agents.squad_id (home column, one per agent) and the memberships join table (many per agent). peers read only the home column.

measured_live_before_fix.why_that_matters: the four invisible agents were the gate agent, the flight coordinator and the lead — the exact agents this seat had been working with all night

defect_found_and_fixed.fix: LEFT JOIN memberships ON (agent_id, squad_id) with OR a.squad_id — a union, not a swap. Swapping would be the mirrored bug: createAgent writes a home-squad membership row, but only for agents created through that path, so older or hand-repaired agents have a home squad and no row.
defect_found_and_fixed.edge_labelling: each row now carries via: ['membership' | 'home_squad' | both] and membership_capability, so the edge states why it exists

falsification.method: reverted the query to its pre-change form and re-ran
falsification.result: kill-witness reports the joined agent as undefined; roster returns 2 of 3 — the live 22-vs-26 in miniature
falsification.why_that_is_correct: those two guard the MIRRORED bug (memberships-only dropping home-squad agents), which the old code did not have
falsification.contaminated_first_attempt: the first falsification run left mem.capability in the SELECT while removing the JOIN, so all six failed on a SQL error rather than on the missing peer. A red test for the wrong reason is not evidence. Recorded rather than discarded; the numbers above are from the clean re-run.

defect_found_and_fixed.test_discipline: tests/mcp-peers-membership.test.ts uses createSqliteD1 + applyAllMigrations. The pre-existing tests/mcp-peers.test.ts keeps its own mock for scoping/liveness, but that mock filters rows by squad_id and therefore cannot express this question at all — it would have reported the defect as correct.

surface_built.gap_closed: reachability was observable only by attempting a write. When gate verdicts stopped arriving directly and had to be hand-carried by Loom, no agent could ask the pot why — the answer existed only as the error string of a message you had to send to find out.
surface_built.not_a_scan_surface: single named target; no list, wildcard or squad sweep. Per Athena Q2 condition.

oracle_property.requirement: a read-only diagnostic must never be a wider oracle than the write it describes
oracle_property.implementation: for a non-admin, every failure collapses to send_target_not_visible, mirroring sendToRef's #401 existence-oracle closure; the resolved target is never echoed when unreachable, since slug/squad in the payload would leak existence even with the reason collapsed
oracle_property.falsification: injecting the leak (returning the specific project reason to a non-admin) turns the collapse test red with 'project_archived' where 'send_target_not_visible' was required

project_arm.why_it_is_not_a_thin_wrapper: the exported resolveVisibleSendTarget implements only case (a), squad visibility. sendToRef additionally honours case (b): when (a) fails but a projectId is present, validateMessageProjectAccess is the authority. A wrapper over the exported primitive alone would have answered 'cannot reach' about the exact project-scoped path currently carrying gate verdicts to this seat — certifying the human relay as permanent.
project_arm.placement: checkSendReachability lives beside sendToRef in messages.ts so the two cannot drift about who can reach whom

my_own_error_corrected.what_i_claimed_to_athena: send already returns the distinguishable pair (send_target_not_visible vs recipient_not_found) to any authenticated caller, therefore can_reach returning the same vocabulary leaks nothing new
my_own_error_corrected.why_it_is_false: for a non-admin, messages.ts collapses every failure to send_target_not_visible. recipient_not_found and recipient_ambiguous are reachable only when authz.isAdmin.
my_own_error_corrected.consequence_if_unnoticed: Athena's Q2 ruling inherited the bad premise. Had the vocabulary shipped as described, can_reach would have been a NEW oracle handing non-admins a distinction send deliberately refuses them.
my_own_error_corrected.reported: seq 3358, before building on the ruling

judgement_calls_needing_a_second_lens: can_reach returns 200 for an honest 'no'. A 403 would make the negative indistinguishable from 'you may not ask', which is the failure this tool removes — but it does mean an unreachable answer is cheap to obtain repeatedly. Whether that needs Athena's rate wall is unresolved.

The hint naming project_id when the squad arm failed tells the caller a lever exists. It names no project and confirms no relationship, but it is still a nudge that the project surface is worth probing.

All four commits sit on one branch because this cloud seat is pinned to one push branch. Both gates asked for splits. Each commit is independently cherry-pickable, but that is a workaround, not compliance, and it is flagged as such rather than presented as done.
